meta.title: Albion Online Artifact Foundry: expected value per roll
meta.description: Expected value of rolling Runes, Souls, Relics or Avalonian shards in the Albion Online Artifact Foundry: cost, profit, worst and best case and chance of losing, by tier.

page.title: Artifact Foundry
page.description: Each roll gives one random artifact from the chosen pool, all equally likely. Here you see whether it pays off and how much you risk.
page.dataCredit: Market data: Albion Online Data Project.

error.title: We couldn’t load the Foundry
error.body: There was a problem reading market prices. It may be temporary: try again.

foundry.heading: Foundry calculator
foundry.note1: Expected value: average payout of each artifact in the pool, net of taxes ({net}% of the price). Artifacts with no price or no sales in 30 days are left out of the average. Loss chance: the share of priced artifacts that sell for less than the roll cost.
foundry.note2: Assumptions: every artifact in the pool is equally likely, and {mixed} fragments per roll in the Mixed pool. Neither comes from the game data dump; the pools do (they are the artifacts whose recipe uses that fragment). Cost uses the cheapest fragment across the cities.
foundry.compareAside: best expected profit across the four pools
foundry.compareCaption: Best expected profit per roll by fragment and tier. Pick a cell to see its detail.
foundry.cellAria: {fragment} T{tier}: {sign, select, gain {gains} other {loses}} {amount} in the {pool} pool
foundry.verdictNoPrice: There is no {fragment} price in any city, so we can’t calculate cost or profit. Below you can see what each artifact in the pool is worth.
foundry.verdictNoSales: No artifact in the {pool} pool sold in the last 30 days, so there is no expected value to compare with the cost.
foundry.verdictDetail: expected value {expected} − cost {cost} · loses {loss} of the time · worst {worst}, best {best}
